title: Unable to correctly switch CameraFeed on Android apps.
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible under:
[Play in Editor, or installed build (sans Gradle, obviously)]
Quest: 4.5.1-stable; in either standard apps, or OpenXR environments.

[Both One-touch deploy, or exported & installed build]
Win64: v4.6.beta.custom_build [19527c623] (#110720 , 19527c623a441911a386c1cf170a003dde4d5145)
Win64: v4.6.beta-2
Win64: v4.5.1-stable

Seems to go all the way back to the introduction of CameraServer support for Android (post 4.4).

### System information

Godot v4.6.beta2 - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9159) - 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-11800H @ 2.30GHz (16 threads) - 63.75 GiB memory

### Issue description

Once an initial CameraFeed has been set active, even if deactivated and then left for a period first, no other feed activates properly.

### Steps to reproduce

Actually spotted in the proposed camera test demo and reproducible there. But how the more *universal* demo approaches Android permissions, strides bug / compatibility, camera formats - and the default behaviour of selecting CameraFeed[0]! - make things a bit murky to see wrt the problem here. Instead, try my 'MRP' attached below.

Either attach an Android device in Debug mode and one-touch deploy, or export and install APK to one.

I've tested the behaviour on:
* Quest 3 - standard 2D app
* Quest 3 - OpenXR - no vendor plugin (with a slight modification to the MRP project, naturally)
* HammerConstruction2-Thermal
* Samsung Galaxy S20+

... working my way down from my intended use case, backwards, to most basic and likely compatible / consumer gear.

```
###################################################################################################
## What we witness here is that - under Android, certainly - once an initial feed has been set active,
## even if deactivated and then left for a period first, no other feed activates properly;
## 
## Attempting to do so:
## 	-	'active' property is set, but frame_changed signal is not detected to emit.
##	-	set_format returns true, but doesn't actually set the format of any subsequent feed.
##
## If reselecting (and activating) the original feed, that one then behaves as normal.
##
## NOTE: Although *hinted* at in the docs, if CameraServer.monitoring == true, new 
##		camera_feeds_updated.connections() seem to silently fail!
##		Could be related behind-the-scenes to our feed-switch problem?
###################################################################################################
```

See, a video demo with narrative here: https://youtu.be/KWirdEIKQb8

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Again, technically, https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/pull/1225 is MRP enough.
However, my project is likely simpler and more tailored to demonstrating the... bug?

[stuck_camera_feeds.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24390996/stuck_camera_feeds.zip)
